Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT A. Francisco Gold Condominium II EDSA Cor. Mapagmahal St., Diliman Quezon City OFFICE OF THE UNDERSECRETARY FOR LOCAL GOVERNMENT TAPAtNAPA.*XD, Legal Opinion No. 36 s. 2011 JUL b LUCI, Atty. NOEL G. NGOLOB Vice Mayor/Presiding Officer Office of the Sangguniang Bayan Municipality of Itogon, Benguet Dear Atty. Ngolob: This concerns Resolution No. 149 series of 201 1 passed by your Sanggunian and approved by your Mayor requesting ciarification from us and other concerned agencies and instrumentalities of the government on the decrease in the national wealth tax share of your municipality regarding the operation of the San Roque Multi-Purpose Dam Project (SRMDP). Irt response thereto, this Department, after going over the documents furnished us, finds it prudent not to render any opinion on the matter. This is especially true because we are not in possession of other document/s, if any, showing what you claimed as a decrease in the national wealth tax share of your municipality with respect to the operation of the SRMDP and the supposed basis thereof. Further, we note that the SRMDP's dam is located in San Manuel, Pangasinan while its reservoir and watershed are hosted by your municipality. This means that the matter concerns not only your municipality and the province of Benguet but also the municipality of San Manuel, Pangasinan and the province of Pangasinan. At any rate, please be reminded that, insofar as this Department is concerned, Republic Act No. 7160, as amended, otherwise known as the Local Government Code (LGC) of 1991, particularly in Chapter 2, Title 3, Book II thereof, merely provides that the local government units where the national wealth are being developed or utilized shall receive 40% of the proceeds of the national wealth tax and, if the natural resources are located in two or more provinces, or in two or more cities or municipalities, or in two or more barangays, the respective shares of the local government units concerned shall be computed on the basis of the population (70%) and land area (30%). This is also true in the Implementing Rules and Regulations (IRR) of the LGC of 1991, particularly, Part II, Rule XXXII thereof. However, the IRR further provides that the computation of the 40% share of each local government unit shall be submitted by the revenue collecting agencies to the Department of Budget and Management (DBM) and that this Department, in coordination with the Department of Finance (DOF) and in actual consultation with the leagues of local government units, shall monitor the implementation of the rules regarding national wealth tax share. Considering all the foregoing, this Department, at this moment, deems it wise to advise you to seek the DOF's enlightenment on how the 40% share of the aforementioned local government units is computed. Better yet, we wili appreciate if you can provide us complete information, supported by official

document/s, if any, that serves as your basis in claiming that your municipality's national wealth tax share regarding the operation of the SRMDP has been decreased. hope have enlightened you on the matter. Very y Our S, AUSTERE A. PANADERO Undersecretary Is:
